title: UK crowned in a record quarter
gist: World Gold Council reports record Q3 gold ETF inflows of US$31bn with UK-listed funds setting a record and overtaking China as 2026's top country source, even as the gold price and COMEX net longs fell in September.

insights.claim: Global physically-backed gold ETFs took in US$10bn in September, making Q3 a record US$31bn, and holdings rose 67t to a record 4,256t even as AUM fell 7% m/m to US$574bn on a lower gold price.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Western investors are buying the dip; holdings at record despite price weakness.

insights.claim: North American funds drew US$4bn in September and US$12bn in Q3, the first quarterly inflow of 2026, despite a Fed 25bp hike that pushed up Treasury yields and the dollar.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Inflows persisted despite higher opportunity cost, implying diversification demand over rates.

insights.claim: Asian funds added US$2.3bn in September (US$4.9bn in Q3); Chinese funds kept attracting inflows amid weak domestic equities and falling government bond yields.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese ETF demand is a hedge against weak equities.

insights.claim: UK-listed gold ETFs added US$7.5bn in Q3, their strongest quarter on record, and with US$9.5bn y-t-d marginally overtook China as the largest country source of 2026 inflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: UK is the leading source of marginal gold ETF demand.

insights.claim: UK-listed funds saw inflows in 12 of 13 weeks to 25 September, the most consistent run since 2022, coinciding with a rising gilt term premium.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gilt fiscal and inflation worries are feeding gold demand.
insights.quote: sustained investor interest rather than a reaction to a single event

insights.claim: Europe attracted larger gold ETF inflows than North America in Q3, the first time that happened in a quarter with inflows in both since Q2 2021.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Regional flow leadership has shifted to Europe.

insights.claim: Global gold volumes averaged US$423bn per day in September (-2% m/m) while gold ETF trading volumes fell 19% to US$7bn per day.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Lower ETF trading with record holdings suggests a buy-and-hold investor base.

insights.claim: COMEX net longs fell 13% (100t) in September to 654t, with managed money down 84t to 387t and spreading positions down 156t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Futures liquidation diverged from ETF buying and weighed on price.
